prompt: A force of ${{force}}\text{ N}$ acts at ${{angle}}^\circ$ above the horizontal, as shown. What is its horizontal component $F_x$?
teacher_notes: The sine distractor is the vertical component; the force itself and F/cos θ catch students who skip resolving.
explanation: The horizontal component is adjacent to the angle: $F_x=F\cos\theta=({{force}})\cos {{angle}}^\circ\approx{{calc: round(force * cos(angle), 1)}}\text{ N}$. $F\sin\theta$ gives the vertical component, ${{calc: round(force * sin(angle), 1)}}\text{ N}$.
